clinical_subtitle: Often discussed as non-specific / mechanical low back pain
results_header: Here’s what this might relate to
why_it_might_fit: You described back-focused pain that changed with movement or activity — a common pattern discussed in mechanical low-back education.
what_people_notice: Pain or stiffness in the lower back; it may spread toward the buttock.
Moving, bending, or sitting can change how it feels.
Many similar episodes improve over weeks with sensible activity — a clinician still decides what’s right for you.
could_also_be: Non-specific / mechanical low back pain (most common education pattern)
Nerve-root irritation / “sciatica”-type leg pain (see also leg-dominant pack)
Less often: other spinal or referred patterns a clinician would consider
Rare serious causes are why the red-flag check comes first
what_this_is_not: This is not a diagnosis of a “slipped disc” or any specific injury.
Scan findings are common with age and do not always match pain.
A clinician would confirm what’s going on for you.
settle_expectation: Many people with common low-back pain improve over weeks to a few months with sensible activity. Flare-ups and repeat episodes are common.
soft_flags: Disabling pain, work or sleep impact, or not improving after a few weeks of sensible self-care — see a physiotherapist or GP.

trusted_links.label: NICE NG59 — Low back pain and sciatica (guideline depth)
trusted_links.caveat: Pathways can differ from NZ care.
